title: Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Ending Explained: Will There Be a Next Generation Sequel?
content:
The Bleach anime has finally come to an end 22 years after its inception, fulfilling the dreams of fans who have long wanted to see the series reach a satisfying conclusion. The anime’s original run of 366 episodes ended in 2012, but the manga continued until its conclusion in 2016, when fans began demanding an anime adaptation of the final arc. Their wish came true with Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War , which premiered in October 2022. Four years and 50 episodes later, this installment has also come to an end, marking the conclusion of one of the biggest shonen anime series of all time.

Bleach ‘s ending couldn’t have been more perfect , bringing the epic battle against Yhwach to a satisfying conclusion. Ichigo’s final blow, made possible by the crucial elements Yhwach had affected and the combined efforts needed to defeat him, reinforced the idea that unity and collective strength can overcome evil. The series finale then took a step back, depicting the heroes’ lives ten years after Yhwach’s defeat. While everything was as happy as it could be, the series also offered a glimpse of the next generation, laying the foundation for the story to continue.

Bleach Ends With Major Possibilities for the Next Generation

Though the series finale depicted all the happiness fans could have hoped for, it also revealed that remnants of Yhwach’s powers remained. Amid the celebrations, including Rukia receiving the title of captain, the lingering presence of Yhwach’s power suggested that something was still to come. However, the threat was immediately dismissed by none other than Ichigo and Orihime’s son, Kazui. In a surprising reveal, Ichigo’s son was shown to be a Soul Reaper, and the ease with which he eliminated the threat implied that, much like his father, he was special and incredibly powerful. Meanwhile, another element laying the foundation for the future is Rukia and Renji’s daughter, Ichika Abarai.

Ichika’s encounter with Kazui feels like another fateful meeting, reminiscent of the first encounter between Rukia and Ichigo in the series’ opening episode . This suggests the possibility of a new generation with fresh threats and storylines for Bleach to explore. Much like Naruto , which introduced a sequel featuring Naruto’s son as its protagonist, Bleach could follow a similar path. Considering both are among the biggest shonen franchises of all time, Bleach could explore the same approach. Even if a sequel has not been confirmed, the anime series could still expand in other ways.

One possibility lies in a one-shot that author Tite Kubo released in 2021, which introduced the Hell arc . The story featured an intriguing event in which characters such as Yamamoto, Unohana, and Ukitake were trapped in Hell because of a specific ritual. As this arc comes next chronologically, and recent changes in the anime have also hinted at it , there are more than enough reasons to believe this story could come to life as well. Announcements about the franchise’s future and what lies ahead could also arrive soon at Jump Festa 2027.

Bleach ‘s Future Will Be Unveiled Very Soon

Shonen Jump’s biggest event of the year, Jump Festa , will take place on December 19–20. The Bleach anime has secured a special spot at the event, with a Jump Stage scheduled for December 20. Considering that the anime has only recently concluded, the fact that Bleach is still getting a stage is a big deal. The event often discusses the future of franchises, meaning there is more than a chance that something new for the series could be announced. Meanwhile, another event is also coming next year.

BLEACH FES is a two-day event celebrating the end of the TV anime series, scheduled for February 27–28, 2027. If Jump Festa isn’t where fans receive new information, this second event could certainly be the place. As for what could actually be unveiled, whether a sequel or something else, it is still difficult to say. Perhaps Bleach could follow the modern trend of adapting its Hell arc one-shot into a movie, much like other major franchises have done in recent years. The revival of Bleach through Thousand-Year Blood War has been one of the franchise’s biggest achievements, and there is reason to believe the anime could expand with a movie or sequel soon. For now, fans will have to wait patiently for these major events.

title: TANUKI: Pon's Summer Game Launches on November 10
content:
Kyoto-based indie studio Denkiworks announced during Nintendo 's Indie World Showcase on Wednesday that its TANUKI: Pon's Summer game will launch for Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox Game Pass, and PC via Steam on November 10.

The Tanuki Festival is just a month away, and the shrine is in disrepair. Follow Pon, a well meaning, if a bit lazy Tanuki with a part-time job at the Post Office, as he works to restore the shrine before summer ends. Deliver packages, make friends, and get the shrine ready for the big festival!

Players take control of post office delivery animal Pon as they deliver letters across town, build their shrine, and collect hats.

title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Showrunner Talks Season 2 Ending, Future Plans & More
content:
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners has kicked off a new era of its franchise with the release of a new season of episodes with Netflix, and ComicBook got to dig into all sorts of spoiler filled details about the season with the showrunner behind it all. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 picks up after the end of the original series and introduces fans to a whole new set of characters making their own way through Night City . But while its new characters and a new story, it shares a lot of thematic similarities with the first series.

That’s the core of what Cyberpunk: Edgerunners showrunner Bartosz Sztybor wanted to be sure to emphasize when speaking to ComicBook about the new season . Digging into all of the spoilery details about putting the new episodes together, crafting each of these characters, and the conversations between the themes of both seasons, Sztybor opened up about everything that went into it all. Read on for our full interview below (which has been edited for length and clarity).

When Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Started Coming Together

NICK VALDEZ, COMICBOOK: That original [ Cyberpunk: Edgerunners ] series ended on as conclusive of an ending as one could get. So I’m just curious as to how you even approached crafting another story to continue it on. When in the process did you decide to introduce a whole new batch of characters with it? Was it something you had in mind from the very beginning?

BARTOSZ SZYTBOR: Maybe not the very beginning, but while writing scripts for Edgerunners , I already had some stories for other Edgerunners, I would say. There were a few, but I thought the best approach would be to tell a story that will be a mirror and a dialogue. So I’m in a constant dialogue with season one. That’s why Weak is somehow David in reverse. So the idea was in 2021 or even 2020, and then I searched for the right story for the right context.

There was never an option to do a classic proper sequel to resurrect David. No, no, we don’t want to do things like that. But I somehow wanted to show that there are always consequences to your choices and even you can die, but there are still consequences. So that was something that was about what I was thinking constantly with Edgerunners 2.

Speaking to that it’s cool to see that David’s actions in that first series reverberated as it essentially made Arasaka weakened for this exploit. So I wanted to ask about focusing on the Relic Chip and Project Capricorn for this series as a result of that. Was that something you wanted to introduce in this series now that you’ve already helped to establish the Night City world in that first season?

Yes, yes. I mean, a lot of things were somehow born in the process when we were talking what we can use, what we can’t use, what we won’t use. The idea behind Edgerunners was always to somehow mirror things that already happened. So David’s arc and Weak’s arc are somehow similar, but then you have Capri and the Chip, which mirrors V and Johnny Silverhand from the game. And of course the bigger world building approach. So as you said, David’s actions had consequences and what then happened with this world.

On Hiding D’s True Name

Speaking to David and parallels, we have another David here in this series with D. What was the idea behind hiding his name was David? We get that full parallel at the end where he essentially turns into David [Martinez], but I just want to know from your point of view, what the approach to that was?

David, even after dying, there are consequences to what he did. There’s this bigger narrative about those kids with high empathy. But what was super exciting for us was that, again, another parallel, that revenge was also one of the drives for David, and they are a main driver for D. But then we thought, what if he can’t fulfill his revenge? What will happen with him then? And again, what is going to do if he has the possibility to sacrifice?

Because David did one thing, and what I love about the Edgerunners audience is that there is a split. One side of audience thinks that it was a good choice that he sacrificed for love. The other half thinks that, “Oh, it was stupid, he shouldn’t do that.” So that was also another thing that somehow inspired me to write season two, is there glory in sacrifice? So again, that’s as a character, that was those main inspirations, how to create him, what kind of character he is.

You mentioned youth and there’s a lot of youth, especially in this series with Roman, and that’s tapping into the current trend of needing to film things that are happening. And so it is interesting to see that kind of play out here in the sequel. So what was the idea behind Roman and his camera and putting him at the center of this?

There are few things that inspired Roman. One thing is definitely that the creative energy between me and Kai Ikarashi, the director, was amazing. We are both cinephiles, so we wanted to show our love to cinema. The second thing is that in Edgerunners , David and his storyline was rather straightforward. Here you have a few characters, so we needed someone to connect all those characters. The third thing is that it’s another parallel.

David’s story was a story about the end of innocence, so Roman is this one and only innocent character in the whole crew, and this is our way to play with the audience. To suggest that, “Okay, so will it be another story about end of innocence? How will that innocence end for Roman?” But Roman is different than David. You have the same question about innocence in this world, but the outcome may be different because Roman is a different character than David.

Figuring Out Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 ‘s Ending

Speaking to that outcome and parallels, the title for the final episode [“Then Everyone Went Home”] made me worried because I thought it was going to be ironic, considering how that first series ended. But now that we’ve been talking here, it really does fit as a companion and makes the project whole because it’s a hopeful and happy ending. So it seems like that’s what you wanted to get across for these characters, right?

Yeah, yeah, exactly. But for me, maybe I’m a weird person, but for me, season one also has a happy ending. But also about that happy ending, to me, Edgerunners 2 ‘s ending is even more ambiguous than season one’s ending. And for me, it’s so interesting to hear that all the people that saw Edgerunners 2 already are saying that, “Yes, this is a happy ending.” But is it really? I think the audience, after all those nine episodes of violence and sadness, because I think Edgerunners 2 is getting darker much faster than season one, the audience just will take a glimpse of hope as a happy ending. So I really like that this ending is what it is because I think it will give you what you want to get from that story.

That’s the thing because it felt conclusive also. The first season was conclusive in an entirely different way. Character’s fates were clinched, but here it does feel like it’s the end of each of their stories, which was very impressive too. And you mentioned how Weak has a parallel to David, because his whole arc is interesting. He’s Weak Kingsley, and you literally weaken him by stripping him of his modifications at the start. Could you dig into that a little bit more of building him out as a character?

He’s my favorite character. He was the first. I mean, it all started with him. While working on Edgerunners , I had him in the back of my head as a reverse version of David. But then one of my main inspirations for Edgerunners 2 was Léon: The Professional , so I was thinking about that. Another parallel, the relationship between David and Gloria, his mother, that we see the consequences of it, of the way the relationship looked like. But we see that from the perspective of a child, not mother.

So then I thought, let’s now show the relationship between a father and a daughter, but mostly from his perspective and how he needs to rethink who he really is. There was a lot of parallels, a lot of inspirations from movies from the ’90s. This important question that was the final question for David, “Is there glory in sacrifice?” That was also the idea for Weak. I mean, he starts as this super famous merc, but then from episode two, he starts at the bottom. So would he be ready to sacrifice himself as David did in first season?

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 3?

Especially with the scene of him stripping off his jacket, which is him stripping off the crown and the identity before running out to save Talia. Speaking to the Talia aspect of it all too, she feels like the most tragic figure within this. So how did it go just making sure to balance that? Because you’re right, it gets very dark very quickly and it’s because of Talia. She suffers quite a bit.

I think in today’s world, both in pop culture and fashion, the body is such an important thing, and we talk about it a lot. I thought in Cyberpunk ‘s reality, that is our reality times 100, it’ll be even more important. I always had an idea to do something about it, and to do something about a character that is super unhappy about who they are. That’s why she’s somehow similar to Weak, who’s been there, done that in a different way. It’s also another parallel to David who was unhappy with who he was and how he looks. So these were the main inspirations for Talia.

Now as a final question here, I do have to ask with the end of this series, is there a potential for more in the future? Because it feels conclusive in its own way, so I do have to ask if there are other characters you might have in mind to explore?

You never know. There’s a lot of stories to tell in Night City and beyond, so you never know. But not only my, but I think the whole studio’s approach, [CD Projekt RED’s], is that there always needs to be a perfect story and a perfect director, artist, or a studio that will be able to pull off this story. So if the stars align and will be able to create something high quality again, then yes. But if there’s no perfect story or no perfect director with his unique or her unique voice, then maybe it will be just two Edgerunners .

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is now streaming with Netflix worldwide.

title: Bana Yoshida Launches New Kui Otoko no Majо̄ to Kyūseishu Manga
content:
Square Enix 's Monthly Big Gangan magazine announced on X (formerly Twitter ) on Monday that Bana Yoshida will launch a new manga titled Kui Otoko no Majо̄ to Kyūseishu ( The Man-Eating Witches and The Seed of Salvation ) in the third 2027 issue on February 25.

The magazine teases the series with the description: "The girl magicians were aiming for my 'seed!?' Presented with extremely beautiful artwork, a multi-heroine love fantasy!"

Yoshida and Yūki Yaku launched a spinoff manga of Yaku's Bottom-tier Character Tomozaki light novels titled Minami Nanami Wants to Shine on Shogakukan 's Manga ONE app in July 2020. The series was also published in Shogakukan 's Sunday GX . Shogakukan published the third and final compiled book volume in July 2023. Yen Press publishes the series in English and shipped the third volume in February 2024.

Shogakukan published the Bottom-tier Character Tomozaki ( Jaku-chara Tomozaki-kun ) light novel series with illustrations by Fly in May 2016. The novels have ranked in the top 10 of the ranking for top light novels in Takarajimasha 's Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! (This Light Novel Is Amazing!) guidebook from 2017 to 2019. The novels started their last stage in the 11th volume in March 2023. Shogakukan shipped the 13th volume in January 2024. The company also released two short story compilation volumes as volumes 6.5 and 8.5.

The novels ended with the 12th volume on October 16.

The company also released two short story compilation volumes as volumes 6.5 and 8.5.
The novels ended with the 12th volume on October 16.

title: Urban Myth Dissolution Center, Schrödinger's Call Games Get Switch 2 Releases
content:
Shueisha Games announced during Nintendo 's Japanese Indie World 2026 livestream on Wednesday that the Urban Myth Dissolution Center and Schrödinger's Call games have both launched for Nintendo Switch 2 on the same day. An upgrade pack from the respective Nintendo Switch version is available for each game.

The Switch 2 edition of Urban Myth Dissolution Center adds features for the Joy-Con 2 mouse controls, such as a gallery to revisit the game's artwork at any time.

The Switch 2 edition of Schrödinger's Call adds HD graphics and raises the framerate to 60 fps.

Urban Myth Dissolution Center launched forSwitch, PlayStation 5, and PC via Steam in February 2025. The game launched for iOS and Android mobile devices in March. Emi Ishikawa launched a manga adaptation of the game in Shueisha 's Ribon magazine in April 2025.

Schrödinger's Call launched for Switch and PC via Steam on May 28.

title: New Shonen Jump Anime Revival Raises Concerns With Sudden Schedule Change
content:
A major Shonen Jump anime revival now airing new episodes this Fall has raised concerns about the state of its production with the sudden announcement of a recap episode coming next. It’s been a strong new Fall of anime releases thus far as fans have gotten to see all sorts of new favorites making their debuts this past month, but some have had fans waiting longer than others. That’s especially true for the anime adaptation of Toshiaki Iwashiro’s Psyren , 19 years after the manga’s original debut.

Psyren was cancelled within the pages of Shonen Jump back in 2010, and 16 years later the franchise has made its return with a new anime revival airing its episodes this Fall. There have been only four episodes of the new series released thus far, but there’s now a big concern over how it’s coming along as the series has announced that next week it will be airing a recap episode instead of another new release. And a recap this early into the anime’s run is a bit troubling.

Psyren Confirms Sudden Recap Episode With Episode 5 Delay

While it’s not necessarily the case with each production, usually when an anime airs a recap episode in place of a new episode, it’s because the team behind the scenes needs more time to develop the next proper new release. That might not be the case here, but it’s concerning because of how soon into the anime’s run that we’re getting one . This doesn’t seem to be one of those cases where special programming in Japan is changing the schedule for the next episode, and bumping it in favor of something more important (which happens quite often).

With only four episodes, it’s also not a lot of material to recap. Given that the first few episodes have also been divisive for how its brought the manga to life thus far, it’s certainly not going to look good for the bigger picture of the experience on a whole . This is the first recap episode for the series, and is likely going to be far from the last before it’s all over. Psyren has yet to confirm how many episodes it was planning to run for, but we’ll have to see how it works out as the series continues through its run for the Fall.

What to Know for Psyren

Katsumi Ono is serving as director on Psyren with animation production handled by Satelight. Shin Yoshida is handling its scripts, Akira Okuma is designing the characters, and Takashi Ohmama, Tatsuhiko Saiki, Shu Kanematsu are composing the music. Original series creator Toshiaki Iwashiro is working closely with the anime team on the new revival, and it’s been teased to be a complete adaptation of the original series’ 100 chapters. Which could end up being a major move forward for Shonen Jump on a whole .

If this cancelled Shonen Jump series is able to find a new life and success with its anime revival, then it opens the door for even more adaptations of other cancelled classics like it. That’s also what makes its production concerns even more troubling because it started out on such a great first impression, but hopefully it’s not a sign of a worse future to come. How are you feeling about the Psyren anime revival so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Good Smile Company Announces Data Breach of Online Store
content:
Good Smile Company announced on Monday that an "unauthorized third party" gained access to personal and other information to members of its online store from October 19-22. The information includes member names, gender, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, order information, and some credit card information, which include the card brand, the last four digits of a used credit card, as well as expiration date. The company noted that the cardholder's name, any card number digits besides the last four, and the security code for credit cards are not included.

The announcement verifies the earlier preliminary announcement the company made on October 23 last week when the company discovered the breach and announced it to users.

The company took the online store down when it discovered the breach on October 23, and is currently investigating the incident. Good Smile Company claimed that it has since "strengthened system security," and added that it has removed the vulnerability that it identified as the cause for the security breach. The company has also reported the incident to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission, in accordance with Japanese law.

Good Smile is a video game developer, hobby and toy merchandise manufacturer, anime producer, and online retail company. The company's signature toy lines are the popular Nendoroid and Figma figure lines. Nendoroid figures are small figures of anime, manga, and pop culture characters that are portrayed in a super-deformed style, and may have limited poseability and swappable faces. Figma is an action figure line of anime, manga, and pop culture characters that focuses on high articulation and poseability.

title: Solo Leveling: Ragnarok Confirms Return From Hiatus With New Season & Artist (First Look Revealed)
content:
Solo Leveling: Ragnarok went on a hiatus in January this year after its Season 2 finale. After several months, the manhwa finally confirmed its return with a brand new artist for the upcoming season. The official X handle of D&C Webtoon dropped the first look at the Solo Leveling: Ragnarok Season 3 cover along with a confirmation that a new illustrator will be in charge of the series from now on. Written by Daul, this series serves as the official spin-off of the original Solo Leveling franchise. It started out as a novel before getting its webtoon adaptation, which became a massive hit. The main reason why the hiatus lasted this long is that the lead artist, JIN, was replaced following his enlistment in the mandatory military service.

Since the military service typically lasts for 18-21 months, the publishers couldn’t wait that long for JIN’s return. Additionally, webtoon artists often take months of breaks between seasons to prepare for the weekly serialization. However, while the hiatus between the first and second seasons only lasted a few months, Season 3 went through some major changes . However, while the webtoon series has confirmed its return with a new season, the release date hasn’t been revealed yet.

What to Expect From Solo Leveling: Ragnarok Season 3

While the first two seasons of the webtoon and the light novel are available to read in Tapas for international fans, the platform announced it will shut down in March next year. Not to mention that starting from October this year, fans can’t buy inks on the platform to read new series. Luckily, the webtoon is also available on Tappytoon, where we can expect Season 3 to land. The series will be released on Korean platforms first, and the English release will take at least a few weeks or even months.

The first two seasons of the webtoon have barely adapted 70 chapters from the novel, which means that the story is still in its initial phase. Season 3 won’t be the final season of the series, but the story will start getting more intense from here on out, especially after the cliffhanger in the Season 2 finale. The season ends with Ammut threatening Ganga and Pia during the intense battle. The biggest problem is that Ammut’s strength is on par with Suho’s, so his appearance gives the Monarchs’ descendants a huge edge in the battle.

Solo Leveling: Ragnarok Deserves Its Own Anime

While the webtoon is still in the initial phase of the story, the novel has long since concluded. Not to mention that the series is more than enough popular to get its own anime adaptation. The only thing holding it back is that the original anime hasn’t fully adapted the entire story yet. Solo Leveling Season 2 ended after wrapping up the Jeju Island Arc. While a sequel movie has been officially confirmed , there are no updates on its release. However, it won’t be surprising if Ragnarok also got its own anime adaptation after the main story. Solo Leveling: Ragnarok not only introduces new additions to the cast but also brings back some of the most beloved characters from the original story to keep fans hyped. Additionally, the series is more than popular enough, with a huge global fanbase who will be thrilled to follow the journey of Jinwoo’s son.

Are you excited for Solo Leveling: Ragnarok Season 3? Head down to the comments to share your thoughts on the new art style.

title: Bleach Anime Says Goodbye to Ichigo With Special Video After Finale – Watch
content:
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has ending the TV anime’s run after 22 long years, and a special video is helping to say goodbye after Ichigo Kurosaki’s long journey. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has capped off the anime with its final episode after 22 long years, and with it had seen Ichigo and the others heading off into a peaceful future ten years after the fight with Yhwach . It’s an ending that fans have waited a decade to see in action, but it’s still an unfortunate goodbye for the hero.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War had been leading to the debut of its final episodes with a series of special visuals showing off all of Ichigo’s transformations over the decades. Going from the very beginning with the Substitute Soul Reaper Arc all the way through to the end of the series , a special new video has been released after the final episode as a way to fully say goodbye to Ichigo after all this time. You can check it out below to see all of Ichigo’s respective forms over the years.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Says Goodbye to Ichigo After 22 Years

“Bleach The Stories” had been the official name for a slate of special visuals that had been released through the course of the final season that showcased all of Ichigo’s looks over the years. Not only going back to the beginning with his initial transformation into a Soul Reaper seen in the first episode ( which also got a cool remake in the anime’s finale ), but it ends with Ichigo’s final look in the series following its ten year timeskip to cap it all off. It’s been a very long journey for Ichigo, and even longer for those fans waiting to see it all.

The final look for Ichigo sees him living at peace together with Orihime, and the two have had a son of their own named Kazui . It’s teased that their son is now stronger than the both of them with an affinity to see souls like his parents, but that’s where the anime ultimately ends. It’s a fun gag to tease what kind of future could be next for their child, but it’s unfortunately the end of the anime for now. But as fans know about Bleach itself, it’s not the actual end of Tite Kubo’s manga story.

Is Bleach’ s Hell Arc Going to Get an Anime?

As part of the celebration for the manga’s 20th anniversary five years ago, Tite Kubo returned for an official one-shot manga that actually picked up from the events of Bleach ‘s original finale. This new one-shot took place even further in the timeline from the finale, and revealed a whole new crew of Soul Reapers. At the same time, it ended with the tease of a whole new arc to come “No Breathes From Hell” with new enemies from a brand new Hellish region of villains waiting to make their move.

Although the Bleach anime has ended its main TV run, there is always a potential to see this one-shot animated someday. With Kubo teasing an interest in continuing the story with a new arc, fans have been waiting all these years for this to actually happen. Now with the anime at an end, it’s now properly cleared the runway for a sequel in the future. It’s just a matter of waiting however long it takes to happen. How do you feel seeing Ichigo say goodbye with Bleach after all these years? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Bakudo Action Game's Trailer Reveals Switch 2 Version, 2027 Release
content:
Shueisha Games announced during the Japanese Nintendo Indie World Showcase on Wednesday that Sayil Games' Bakudo game will get a Nintendo Switch 2 version. The game will launch for both Switch 2 and PC via Steam in 2027. The company streamed a trailer:

The game's Steam page describes the story:

In BAKUDO, strength is everything. Soliris Academy is the prestigious school where everyone chasing the title of top Corestriker comes to test themselves. Yuria arrives there following a lead on her missing father, but breaks the rules during her entrance exam to save a fellow examinee in danger, and her admission is revoked on the spot. That's when Aria appears, the strongest student at Soliris Academy and the one who stands atop its ranked Stellar Eight. She hands Yuria an ultimatum: defeat the Stellar Eight within ten days, or leave the academy for good. With her partner Evie at her side, Yuria races to meet that challenge. But behind the academy's glittering reputation lies a secret that could decide the fate of the world.

The sci-fi action game centers on battles in which players throw balls as part of combat.
